try: Open a quote on your phone: it opens as the document, not the editor
how:
1. On your phone (the Network address from chapter 12), tap "Tools" in the bottom bar › "Quotes"
2. Tap the card "Olivia Martinez" (OM-10001, Draft)
3. Read the top of the screen, then scroll to the end
expect: The quote opens as a screen, not the editor: a back arrow, "Olivia Martinez" with "OM-10001 · Whole-home renovation" under it, ⋮ at the right. Under that a hero: the Draft chip, the amount large, the number of lines, "Valid until …", the GST line, and Olivia with Call and WhatsApp buttons. One "Next" line says what this quote needs. Then the quote's sections as cards (each folds on a tap), then rows for Payment schedule, Files, Terms and conditions and Signature, each with a one-line summary. A foot stays at the bottom with "Edit" and "Send ▾". Nothing scrolls sideways.
in10: Different from 1.0: a quote on a phone opens as the document; the editor comes on Edit

try: Edit is a list of sections, one at a time
how:
1. Tap "Edit" in the foot
2. Read the list
3. Tap "Items"
4. Tap the back arrow at the top left
5. Tap "Done"
6. Tap "Edit" again, then press your phone's own Back
expect: Edit opens a list: General info, Items (with the count), Payment schedule, Files (with the count), Terms and conditions, Additional notes, Signature — each with a one-line summary of what it holds. Items opens as its own screen with a bar at the top (← · "Items" · "16 lines · S$…"). The arrow returns to the list; Done returns to the quote screen. The phone's Back goes back one step, never out of the quote (the address carries the step).
in10: Different from 1.0: one section at a time on a phone

try: Items are cards; a line opens as a sheet
how:
1. Edit › Items
2. Tap the "Bathrooms" section card, then tap it again
3. Scroll: the open section's card holds at the top
4. Tap a line
5. Change the quantity and watch the Total; tap "More"
6. Tap "Done"
expect: A section card folds and unfolds its lines. Each line is a card: the name, "44 sqft × S$102 · Purchase" and its total. A line opens as a sheet with Quantity, Unit, Unit price, a live Total, Kind and Description; the Total changes as you type; More shows cost, markup, discount, GST, room, category, section label, vendor, link and image. Done closes it and the card reads the new figures. A strip stays pinned at the bottom: Subtotal · GST · Total with "Adjust" (entity, discounts, GST, rounding) and "Breakdown" (by category). No Column settings, Row density or Expand on the phone.
in10: Different from 1.0: cards and a two-layer sheet instead of a twelve-column grid

try: A line's ⋮, Remove with Undo, two lines at once, and adding
how:
1. On a line card, tap ⋮
2. Tap "Remove", then "Undo" in the snackbar
3. Hold a card until it ticks, then tap a second card
4. Read the bar, then tap "Clear"
5. Tap "+ Add to Bathrooms" at the end of that section
6. Tap "Add item" at the top
expect: The ⋮ has five rows: Duplicate, Mark as optional, Move to section ›, Remove, More…. Remove takes the card away with a snackbar and Undo brings it back. Holding selects: the bar shows the count with Clear, then Move to section, Delete and ⋯; the pinned total lifts above the bar. "+ Add to Bathrooms" adds a line inside that section and opens its sheet; "Add item" adds one at the end and opens its sheet. Both appear in place when Done is tapped.
in10: Different from 1.0: every remove has Undo; a long press selects

how:
1. Back to the list (← then the list) › "Payment schedule"
2. Tap the first payment
3. Type 15 in the share box and watch the amount
4. Tap "Done"
5. Tap the payment again › "Remove", then "Undo"
expect: Each payment is a card: its name over the description, the amount over "10% · On Approval". The card opens a sheet: name, description, share and amount side by side (typing 15% fills the amount of 15% of the quote's total), the due as "On approval · On a date", Remove at the foot's start and Done. Done writes the change and the card reads "15% · On Approval". Remove takes the card away with Undo; Undo brings it back.
in10: Different from 1.0: the schedule's row was a six-column grid that cut its words on a phone

try: Terms and conditions open full screen
how:
1. The list › "Terms and conditions"
2. Read the row, then tap it
3. Tap into the text, type a word, tap "B" (Bold)
4. Tap "Done"
expect: The section is one row: "n clauses · shown to the client" over the first lines of the text. Tapping it opens a full-screen editor with the tools as big buttons in two rows (each easy to hit, no scrolling toolbar), Write with AI at the foot's start and Done. What you type saves by itself. Done returns to the row, which now shows your word.
in10: Different from 1.0: the text is not an open editor in the middle of a long page

try: The quote's ⋮, Version History as a sheet, and the snackbar over it
how:
1. Done, back on the quote screen tap ⋮ at the top right
2. Read the groups, then tap "Version History"
3. Tap "Revise — start version 2"
4. Tap "Close"
expect: The ⋮ is a sheet with its rows grouped under Look, Change, Share and Export — everything the desktop has, and no key hints. Version History opens as a bottom sheet with Close in its foot. On a never-sent Draft, Revise answers with a snackbar explaining that a draft is edited, not revised — and the snackbar sits above the sheet's foot, never over its Close. Close returns to the quote.
in10: Different from 1.0: menus are bottom sheets on a phone

try: Send for confirmation from your phone
how:
1. On the quote screen tap "Send ▾" › "Send for confirmation"
2. Read the sheet without scrolling
3. Tap "Copy link"
4. Tap "Send via WhatsApp"
expect: The sheet is built to fit the screen: "+65" and the number on one line, the message box tall enough for its whole message, no link row (on an iPhone the body may scroll a little, but the foot with its two buttons stays in reach). Copy link (in the foot) copies the confirmation link with a snackbar; Send via WhatsApp opens WhatsApp with the message and the link ready to send. Back in OpenMaison the quote reads Sent to Client and the foot's primary becomes "Remind".
in10: Same as 1.0: WhatsApp carries the link; the sheet now fits a phone

try: As printed is a viewer; the Preview is the client's reflowed quote
how:
1. On the quote screen scroll to the document and tap "As printed"
2. Swipe left for page 2; double-tap a page; pinch
3. Tap "Fit to width", then the back arrow
4. Open "/quotes/<this quote>/preview" (⋮ › Preview)
5. Tap "Paper" (the "n lines · As printed" row), then ⋮ in the bar
expect: As printed opens a viewer: the head "As printed · OM-10001 · n pages" with Download, the page fitted to the width, a dot per page that follows your swipe, double-tap zooms and "Fit to width" brings it back. The arrow returns to the quote. The Preview page shows the client's quote as cards under one bar (← · Preview · Send ▾); the paper row opens the same viewer. The bar's ⋮ holds Copy preview link, Share PDF, Internal copy, What your client sees and Change template.
in10: Different from 1.0: no A4 shrunk to a phone's width

how:
1. As Germaine (View as), open OM-10001 on the phone: read the foot
2. Tap the primary, confirm, read the foot again
3. As Dane, open the same quote: tap "Approve", then read the foot
4. Open OM-10007 (Serena Koh, Sent to Client): read the foot; set a future "Valid until" in General info and read it again
5. Open OM-10004 (Ryan D’Souza, Signed): read the foot
expect: Germaine's Draft offers "Send" (for approval); once sent, only Edit stays. Dane sees "Approve", then "Send ▾". Serena's quote, past its validity, offers "Revise"; with a future date it offers "Remind", which opens the reminder sheet (a WhatsApp nudge with the confirmation link). Ryan's signed quote offers "Open contract". Every other action is under ⋮.
in10: New in 2.0: the state decides the one filled button

how:
1. Tools › Quotes on the phone
2. Read a card; tap its ⋮
3. Hold a card until it ticks
4. Tap "Filters"
5. Open Olivia's lead › "Quotes" tab
expect: Each card leads with the client's name (bold) and the amount at the right; under them the number and title; then a status chip with its "since" (sent · viewed · due · valid until) and a chevron. The ⋮ offers Open, Copy link, Remind (only while the client holds it), Preview, Change status ›, Archive and Delete. Holding a card selects it and shows the bar. Filters is one sheet of chips. The lead's Quotes tab shows the same cards with the title first.
in10: Different from 1.0: the client leads the card; no checkbox

try: Create a quote on your phone
how:
1. Tools › Quotes › "+"
2. Pick a lead under "Who is this quote for?"
3. Read the four rows; tap "Change" beside the default template, then Back
4. Tap "Blank quote"
expect: The first step asks "Who is this quote for?" with the recent leads first. Then four tall rows: the default template by name ("Starts with …" and Change), Blank quote, Upload a quote, Draft with Maison AI. Change opens the templates as a list (name over its details). Blank quote makes the quote and opens it as the quote screen. From a lead's Quotes tab the rows show at once (the lead is known).
in10: Different from 1.0: the lead first, then four rows

try: A tablet held upright reads like the phone, with more room
how:
1. On a tablet (or the laptop's browser made 768 wide with touch on), open Tools › Quotes
2. Read the table and its right edge
3. Open OM-10001; tap Edit › Items; tap a line
4. Open Olivia's lead › Quotes
expect: The list is a table with Title, Client, Status, Total and Due, the ⋮ frozen at the right (no View button: the title opens), Create Quote as a "+". The quote opens as the quote screen in a wide column; Items are cards and a tapped line opens in a panel at the right (Quantity and Unit price first), the list still scrolling beside it. The lead's Quotes tab hides the quick-links strip to keep the table's room.
in10: Different from 1.0: a default set of columns on a tablet

try: A tablet held sideways: the list beside the section, a working grid
how:
1. Turn the tablet sideways (1024 wide, touch)
2. Open OM-10001 › Edit
3. Tap "Items"; read the grid; tap a Total
4. Tap ⋮ › Column settings › turn "Cost" on; reload
5. Open ⋮ › Preview
expect: Edit keeps the section list as a pane at the left and the open section at the right; a row swaps the section. Items is a grid of Item, Qty, Unit, Unit price and Total that fits without panning; a tap on a Total opens the rest in the panel; Column settings adds Cost with an "internal" caption and remembers it for the tablet only. The Preview's A4 fits the width under one bar.
in10: Different from 1.0: five columns a finger can edit, the rest one tap away

try: The confirmation link on the client's phone
how:
1. Send Serena's quote for confirmation (26.08) and open the copied link on the phone
2. Scroll to the end
3. Tap "View as printed", pinch, then back
4. Tap "Confirm quote"
5. On a tablet held sideways, open the same link
expect: The page starts with a total card (the amount, the lines, valid until, View as printed), then the quote as cards, with a bar that stays at the bottom: "Confirm quote" (tall) and "Ask". View as printed opens the paper in a viewer with pinch. Confirm opens a short sheet: the name, the fine print, Confirm. Sideways on a tablet the card sits above the paper and Confirm keeps its size.
in10: Different from 1.0: Confirm is always within reach
